claim: Cheong Fatt Tze (Blue Mansion) runs two daily 45-minute guided tours at 11am and 3:30pm, capped at 24 people, priced RM25 adults / RM12.50 children under 12.
quote: 2 tours daily at 11am and 3.30pm ... Duration: 45 minutes ... Maximum 24 people per tour ... Adults: RM25.00 ... Children under 12: RM12.50

claim: Ernest Zacharevic returned in September 2024 to personally restore three iconic 2012 George Town murals: 'Children on a Bicycle' (Armenian Street), 'Children on a Chair' (Cannon Street) and 'Boy on a Motorbike' (Ah Quee Street).
quote: THREE iconic murals located on Armenian Street, Ah Quee Street, and Cannon Street in George Town are currently undergoing a restoration process.

claim: Zacharevic's 'Little Children on a Bicycle' mural is on a shophouse wall on Armenian Street within the UNESCO core zone (GPS 5.41468, 100.33823) and uses a real bicycle prop for a 3D effect; painted for the 2012 George Town Festival.
quote: Little Children on a Bicycle is a mural on a wall of a shophouse on Armenian Street, George Town ... GPS: 5.41468, 100.33823 ... painted by London-trained artist Ernest Zacharevic, in conjunction with the 2012 George Town Festival.

claim: Leong San Tong Khoo Kongsi (18 Cannon Square) is open daily 9am-5pm with admission RM10 adults / RM1 children, accessed via an alleyway off 9 Lebuh Cannon.
quote: Open Daily 9 am - 5 pm ... Adults: RM 10 ... Children (ages 5-12): RM 1 ... 18, Cannon Square, George Town, 10450 George Town, Pulau Pinang

claim: The Clan Jetties along Weld Quay are free to visit and Chew Jetty (the most-visited) asks tourists to come 9am-9pm; other surviving jetties include Lee, Tan, Lim and Yeoh.
quote: Chew Jetty is the most popular of the Clan Jetties for tourists, and they've politely requested that tourists only visit between the hours of 9am to 9pm. Visiting the Clan Jetties is completely free of charge

claim: Chew Jetty holds a 3.7/5 TripAdvisor rating across 3,046 reviews; visitors praise the stilt houses and sunset views but warn it has grown commercialised and can be walked end-to-end in 15-20 minutes.
quote: Overall Rating: 3.7 of 5 stars (3,046 reviews) ... You can walk in and out in 15-20 minutes unless you want to stop at all the small shops

claim: Pinang Peranakan Mansion at 29 Church Street is a restored late-19th-century Baba-Nyonya townhouse open 9:30am-5pm daily, with around 1,000 antiques on display; standard adult admission is RM20.
quote: The Pinang Peranakan Mansion is typically open from 9:30 am to 5:00 pm daily ... Entrance fee is RM20 for adults ... 29, Church Street, 10200 George Town

claim: Kapitan Keling Mosque, founded in the late 18th century by Indian-Muslim traders and redesigned in 1916 in British Mughal Revival style with yellow domes, anchors Jalan Masjid Kapitan Keling — the 'Street of Harmony' — and is free to enter (donations welcome).
quote: The Kapitan Keling Mosque, built in the 18th century, is the oldest formally established mosque by Indian Muslim traders in George Town. By 1916, it was redesigned in a British Mughal Revival style with iconic minarets and ornate yellow domes

claim: Sri Mahamariamman Temple on Lebuh Queen, built in 1833, is Penang's oldest Hindu temple, famed for its elaborate gopuram of god/goddess sculptures; open 6:30am-noon and 4:30-9pm daily.
quote: The oldest Hindu temple in Penang, it was built in 1833 and features sculptures of gods and goddesses over its main entrance and facade. The temple is open daily from 6:30 am - 12:00 noon and 4:30 pm - 9:00 pm

claim: The Goddess of Mercy Temple (Kuan Yin Teng) on Pitt Street/Jalan Masjid Kapitan Keling was founded in 1800 by Hokkien and Cantonese immigrants and is open roughly 7am-6pm daily, making it the oldest Chinese temple in George Town.
quote: The Goddess of Mercy Temple was founded in 1800 by early Chinese immigrants from the Hokkien and Cantonese communities, constructed at a cost of $3,700. The temple remains open daily from approximately 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

claim: Kapitan Keling Mosque, Goddess of Mercy Temple, Sri Mahamariamman Temple and St George's Anglican Church sit within walking distance along Jalan Masjid Kapitan Keling — the 'Street of Harmony' — illustrating UNESCO's multi-religious citation.
quote: These three temples and the Kapitan Keling Mosque are located on Kapitan Keling Street (Lebuh Kapitan Keling), also known as the 'Street of Harmony,' showcasing Penang's unique spirit of religious coexistence.

claim: The Penang State Museum & Art Gallery on Lebuh Farquhar is still in restoration — phase one finished May 2024, with phase two expected to take a further six to nine months, so the main museum was closed through late 2024 (art gallery and research unit remained open).
quote: Phase one of restoration works on the iconic Penang State Museum and Art Gallery in Farquhar Street was completed ... Phase two, the final phase of the restoration work, was expected to be completed between six and nine months

claim: A brand-new Penang History Museum opened on Bishop Street in March 2025 — an RM3-million attraction using holograms, AI-driven displays and recreated street scenes to dramatise immigrant, British-colonial and pre-war George Town history.
quote: RM3 million has been spent to make, decorate and install various structures to depict the early era of immigrants, British rule, places of interest in the yesteryear and many more. The museum had a soft opening in March 2025

claim: Armenian Street (Lebuh Armenian) is the densest stretch of the UNESCO core zone, packed with shophouses, the 'Kids on Bicycle' mural, Cheah Kongsi, Choo Chay Keong Temple, metal-rod 'caricature' sculptures (Too Narrow, Procession, Then & Now) and a Saturday-evening street fair.
quote: you can see Chinese temples and clan houses such as Cheah Kongsi and Choo Chay Keong Temple, famous street art murals like 'Kids on Bicycle', the umbrella alley or shophouses ... The Armenian Street Fair takes place every Saturday evening

claim: George Town's UNESCO inscription (2008) defines a core zone bounded by the sea and Lebuh Acheh, Lebuh Carnarvon and Lebuh Melayu, covering ~109.38 ha of pre-war shophouses, religious buildings and clan jetties.
quote: Heritage Zones - George Town

claim: Gurney Drive Hawker Centre hosts 50+ stalls along the seafront and is open daily from late afternoon to 1am; recommended stalls include #71/#107 for char kway teow and #79 for asam laksa.
quote: Gurney Drive Hawker Centre... 50+ stalls along Penang's northern seafront promenade, daily late afternoon through 1 AM. Stalls 71 or 107 serve Char Kway Teow... Stall 79 serves Assam Laksa

claim: Penang Road Famous Jin Kor Char Kuey Teow, located inside Joo Hooi Cafe on Penang Road, carries a Michelin Bib Gourmand and is a celebrity-favored CKT stall in George Town.
quote: Penang Road Famous Jin Kor Char Kuey Teow, PENANG – Popular With Celebrities With Michelin Bib Gourmand (In Joo Hooi Cafe)

claim: The legendary Air Itam Laksa stall by Ayer Itam market now opens only Saturday and Sunday 11am–6pm; founder Uncle Seong (Ang Kak Seong) passed away in April 2026 at 77 and the family is continuing the 70-year-old stall.
quote: Uncle Seong (Ang Kak Seong)... passed away in April 2026 at the age of 77... Opening Hours: Saturday & Sunday ONLY | 11:00 AM – 6:00 PM

claim: Nasi Kandar Line Clear at 177 Jalan Penang (junction of Chulia Street and Penang Road) operates 24 hours and has been a fixture since 1947.
quote: Nasi Kandar Line Clear Original

claim: Line Clear has faced repeated complaints in recent years about overcharging tourists, with reports of plates billed at RM57; locals advise asking for prices before ordering.
quote: reports of tourists being charged significantly more, including charges of RM57 for a plate

claim: The 2025 Michelin Guide for Kuala Lumpur & Penang named 56 Bib Gourmand eateries including 12 new entries; new Penang additions are BM Yam Rice, Laksalicious, Lum Lai Duck Meat Koay Teow Th'ng, Ravi's Famous Apom Manis, Serabai Istimewa, Super Star Koay Teow Soup and Winn's Cafe.
quote: In Penang, the inspectors selected BM Yam Rice, Laksalicious, Lum Lai Duck Meat Koay Teow Th'ng, Ravi's Famous Apom Manis, Serabai Istimewa, Super Star Koay Teow Soup and Winn's Cafe

claim: Siam Road Char Koay Teow holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand and is recognised in the Michelin Guide for its charcoal-wok-fried CKT.
quote: Siam Road Char Koay Teow – George Town - a MICHELIN Guide Restaurant

claim: Siam Road Charcoal Char Kway Teow trades from a roadside cart at 82 Jalan Siam Tue–Sat roughly noon–6:30pm and is closed Mondays and Sundays; waits can exceed an hour at peak.
quote: open Tuesday to Saturday from 12pm-6:30pm and is closed on Mondays and Sundays

claim: The Chulia Street Night Hawker cluster has relocated to Carnarvon Street and is busiest 6:30–8:30pm; Mother & Son Wantan Mee (nearly 50 years old) is a standout, with CKT plates RM8–9.
quote: the renowned hawker has shifted to Carnarvon Street... Mother & Son Wantan Mee stall is arguably serving one of the best wantan mee in Penang... small plate of the famed char kuey teow here is priced at RM8

claim: Bridge Street Prawn Noodle (Keo Thau Hokkien Mee) at 533 Lebuh Pantai is a Michelin Bib Gourmand stall known for combining prawn-mee broth with lor-mee gravy; open Tue–Sun 7am–2:30pm, closed Monday.
quote: Bridge Street Prawn Noodle, PENANG – Michelin Bib Gourmand Stall with Hokkien Mee + Lor Mee Gravy Combo

claim: 888 Hokkien Mee at 67-A Lebuh Presgrave has served prawn-noodle soup with pork rib and sambal for 30+ years; daily 3pm–9:30pm, closed Thursdays.
quote: 888 Hokkien Mee serves one of the most flavourful noodle soups in Penang, topped with pork ribs and sambal... operates daily from 3:00 PM to 9:30 PM, except on Thursdays

claim: Penang Road Famous Teochew Chendul on Lebuh Keng Kwee, in business since 1936, sells its signature shaved-ice cendol with coconut milk, gula melaka, kidney beans and pandan jelly noodles; diners eat standing or sit inside the adjacent Joo Hooi Cafe.
quote: Penang Road Famous TeoChew Chendul... started in 1936... Joo Hooi Cafe or bring your bowl and walk 2 stalls down

claim: Seng Thor Coffeeshop on the corner of Carnarvon and Kimberley Street has been frying oh chien (oyster omelette) since the 1930s and is a go-to George Town stop for the dish.
quote: Oyster Omelette (Oh Chien) That You Have To Try In Penang

claim: Penang Foodie's 2025 street-food roundup highlights the canonical local dishes a visitor should target: char kway teow, asam laksa, Hokkien mee, nasi kandar, char hor fun, oh chien, rojak, cendol and ais kacang.
quote: 25 Best Penang Street Food (2025 Edition)

claim: George Town/Penang has exactly two one-Michelin-star restaurants — Au Jardin (Contemporary) and Auntie Gaik Lean's Old School Eatery (Peranakan) — both starred consistently from the 2023 inaugural guide through 2026.
quote: Au Jardin — Contemporary — 1 Michelin star (consistent 2023-2026); Auntie Gaik Lean's Old School Eatery — Peranakan — 1 Michelin star (consistent 2023-2026)

claim: Au Jardin's chef-patron Su Kim Hock runs an 18-seat room at Hin Bus Depot with a vegetable-first ethos and a tasting menu at RM568++ that includes Cognac & Hay Aged Duck and all-cabbage courses.
quote: The ethos of our cooking is always around vegetables. If there's a vegetable and protein combination, it's always vegetables first and then protein.

claim: Au Jardin opens reservations up to three months in advance, operates Thursday–Sunday only, requires a deposit, and enforces a smart-casual dress code (collared shirt, long pants, covered footwear for gentlemen).
quote: Reservations are available up to three months in advance... Shirt with a collar, long pants and covered footwear are required.

claim: Au Jardin describes its cooking as 'La Cuisine Naturelle', is located at The Warehouse @ Hin Bus Depot in Georgetown, and serves Thu-Sun lunch (11:30-14:00) and dinner (17:15-22:00).
quote: Located at The Warehouse @ Hin Bus Depot in Georgetown, Penang... Open Thursday-Sunday for lunch (11:30-14:00) and dinner (17:15-22:00). Maintains a smart dress code requirement.

claim: Auntie Gaik Lean's serves à la carte Peranakan (RM8–RM118 per dish, no tasting menu); signature dishes include Curry Kapitan (RM48), Pie Tee, Gulai Tumis, Nasi Ulam and Bee Koe Moy black glutinous rice; parties of 4+ must reserve with a RM200 nett deposit while parties of 3 or fewer are walk-in only.
quote: A deposit of RM 200 nett per reservation is required... Walk-ins accepted for parties of 3 or fewer on a first-come, first-served basis.

claim: Auntie Gaik Lean's Old School Eatery at 1 Bishop Street, George Town is Malaysia's first homestyle Peranakan eatery to win a Michelin star, awarded in the inaugural 2023 guide; the room is decorated grandma's-living-room style with old radios and porcelain.
quote: Malaysia's first—and Penang's only—homestyle Peranakan eatery awarded a Michelin star in 2022 [for the 2023 guide].

claim: The 2025 Penang Bib Gourmand list contains 32 entries including Teksen (Cantonese), Communal Table by Gēn, Sister Yao's Char Koay Kak, Siam Road Char Koay Teow, Hot Bowl White Curry Mee, Bibik's Kitchen, Ivy's Nyonya, Moh Teng Pheow Nyonya Koay, Tho Yuen and 7 new-for-2025 entries (BM Yam Rice, Laksalicious, Lum Lai Duck Meat Koay Teow Th'ng, Ravi's Famous Apom Manis, Serabai Istimewa, Super Star Koay Teow Soup, Winn's Cafe).
quote: Ah Boy Koay Teow Th'ng, Bibik's Kitchen... Teksen, Thara, Tho Yuen, Wan Dao Tou Assam Laksa, Winn's Cafe

claim: The 2026 Michelin Guide Kuala Lumpur & Penang retained Au Jardin and Auntie Gaik Lean's as Penang's only one-star restaurants; all new 2026 stars (Akar, Terra Dining) went to Kuala Lumpur, leaving Penang with no two-star or three-star restaurants.
quote: Akar and Terra Dining, joining Beta, Chim by Chef Noom, DC by Darren Chin and Molina in Kuala Lumpur; and Au Jardin and Auntie Gaik Lean's Old School Eatery in Penang.

claim: Auntie Gaik Lean's signature Pie Tee and Gulai Tumis showcase eight-spice complexity including fresh saffron, and the restaurant is operated by a small family team in a 30-seat shophouse on Bishop Street with limited service Wed–Sun.
quote: the delicate Pie Tee that crunches like a dream and the Gulai Tumis, where every spoonful sings with the complexity of eight different spices, including the rare brightness of fresh saffron

claim: Au Jardin opened in Penang in 2018 and uses 85 percent locally sourced Malaysian ingredients within a French culinary framework.
quote: menu crafted with 85 percent locally sourced ingredients, seamlessly incorporating French culinary artistry

claim: Penang Hill funicular operates 6:30am to 11:00pm with last trip up at 10:00pm; non-Malaysian adult two-way ticket is RM40 normal lane / RM80 express (fast) lane.
quote: Funicular Service 6.30am – 11.00pm ... Last trip from the Lower Station to the Upper Station (Penang Hill Station) is at 10.00pm ... Normal Lane @ RM 40 / Express Lane @ RM 80

claim: The Habitat Penang Hill rainforest park opens daily 9am to 7pm and includes the Langur Way Canopy Walk and Curtis Crest Tree Top Walk; adult ticket RM60, child RM40.
quote: Entrance to the Habitat Penang Hill costs RM60 ... for an adult ticket and RM40 ... for a child's ticket or a senior citizen ... The Habitat is open Daily 9am – 7pm

claim: Penang Hill and its surrounding 12,481 hectares were officially designated by UNESCO as the Penang Hill Biosphere Reserve on 15 September 2021, making it Malaysia's third biosphere reserve.
quote: The MAB Council officially designated Penang Hill and its surrounding areas as Penang Hill Biosphere Reserve on 15 September 2021 ... comprises 12,481 hectares

claim: Kek Lok Si Temple's annual Chinese New Year light-up features over 200,000 fairy lights and 20,000 lanterns; the temple itself closes at 5:30pm but illuminations switch on at 7:30pm and run till around midnight, best viewed from a distance.
quote: over 200,000 fairy lights and 20,000 Chinese lanterns ... The temple closes at 5:30 pm, and the lights are switched on at 7:30pm until midnight

claim: Penang National Park entry is RM50 for non-Malaysian adults (card only); HQ counter opens 8am–4:30pm with a 1–2pm lunch closure; the Monkey Beach hiking trail is currently open and a boat alternative to Monkey Beach costs RM100 return.
quote: Non-Malaysian adults: RM50 ... Payment method: Card only ... opens from 8:00am to 4:30pm, with an hour's closure for lunch ... The track to Monkey Beach is currently open

claim: Penang National Park's 250-metre Canopy Walkway, a series of hanging bridges through the treetops, remains indefinitely closed for repairs as of 2025–2026.
quote: The Canopy Walkway is a 250 meter series of hanging bridges through the tree tops, but unfortunately it is closed until further notice for repairs

claim: The new Penang Hill Cable Car (2.73km from Botanic Gardens to the summit) is expected to be completed in December 2026, with a further trial period before public opening.
quote: the project is expected to be completed by December 2026 and may take another three months for trial period, dry commissioning and so on before it is opened

claim: As of April 2026 the RM367.2 million Penang Hill cable car project is 28% complete, with deep foundation works and reinforced concrete piles for the multi-storey car park done.
quote: the RM367.2 million Penang Hill cable car project is now 28% complete ... deep foundation works and reinforced concrete piles for the multi-storey car park

claim: ESCAPE Penang in Teluk Bahang is an adventure theme park with Adventureplay, Waterplay and Gravityplay zones; pre-booked online tickets can save up to 30% over walk-in prices.
quote: discounts of up to 30% when you prebook your tickets online compared to walk-in prices

claim: Entopia by Penang Butterfly Farm in Teluk Bahang opens 9am–6pm (last entry 5:30pm), is closed Wednesdays, and tickets start from around RM65.
quote: Entopia Penang opens from 09:00-18:00 ... with the last entry at 17:30 ... Entopia is closed every Wednesday

claim: Tropical Spice Garden in Teluk Bahang opens 9am–6pm Fri–Sun and 9am–4:30pm Mon–Thu, with entry tickets from about RM30.
quote: open daily Friday - Sunday from 9am – 6pm and Mon - Thurs from 9am - 4.30pm, with last admission one hour before closing

claim: Grab e-hailing in Penang is cheap: a typical George Town to Batu Ferringhi ride is around RM14 for ~8km, and George Town to Penang National Park is roughly RM25 for 12km, with night/peak surcharges rarely pushing fares over RM40.
quote: one-way trip from George Town to Batu Ferringhi is just RM 14 ... George Town to Penang National Park is RM 25 for a 12 km ride ... if it costs more than RM40 you'd be very surprised

claim: Batu Ferringhi beach reviews are mixed: water is often murky with jellyfish warnings, sand is coarse, and the area is described as a convenient night-market and watersports stop rather than a pristine beach.
quote: the sea is swimmable but often murky, with jellyfish warnings ... Batu Ferringhi is described as convenient rather than magical—worth a night, not a pilgrimage

claim: The Heritage Core within the UNESCO zone holds over 1,700 protected pre-war shophouses and is the best base for first-time visitors; Little India offers the strongest budget-to-comfort ratio.
quote: The Heritage Core is the architectural heartbeat of George Town's UNESCO World Heritage site, packed with over 1,700 protected pre-war shophouses... For backpackers, this is the neighbourhood where you'll get the most bang for your buck.

claim: Batu Ferringhi sits roughly 30–40 minutes by car from George Town and is the choice for a beach base; most travelers should stay in George Town for food, culture and history.
quote: Batu Ferringhi is Penang's most well-known beach area... located about 30 to 40 minutes' drive from George Town, depending on traffic.

claim: The Eastern & Oriental Hotel was founded by the Sarkies Brothers (Eastern 1884, Oriental 1885, merged 1889); it splits into the restored Heritage Wing and the 132-room Victory Annexe opened in 2013.
quote: The Eastern & Oriental Hotel was established in 1885 in George Town, Penang, Malaysia by the Sarkies Brothers... The Victory Annexe is a separate 132-room tower that replaced the old annex in 2013.

claim: Cheong Fatt Tze – The Blue Mansion offers 18 individually designed rooms around courtyards in the 130-year-old indigo mansion of the 'Rockefeller of the East', with a Qing Suites annexe added in 2025.
quote: The mansion features 18 individually designed rooms surrounding peaceful courtyards. In 2025, The Qing Suites was unveiled—a collection of thirteen suites and a TCM-focused spa within an annexe of the iconic Blue Mansion.

claim: Macalister Mansion is a 1900-era English-style Design Hotels boutique with only 8 luxury rooms, awarded Best Luxury Boutique Hotel in Penang 2025.
quote: Macalister Mansion is a delicately restored Penang boutique heritage hotel with 8 luxury rooms... conferred with the Best Luxury Boutique Hotel in Penang 2025 by Luxury Lifestyle Awards.

claim: Soori Penang, a new 15-room heritage hotel in restored shophouses, debuted in George Town in January 2026.
quote: Soori Penang, a 15-room heritage hotel, debuted in January 2026, composed of restored historic shophouses in George Town, the UNESCO-listed historic capital of Penang Island.

claim: From Penang International Airport (PEN), GrabCar Economy to a George Town hotel runs about RM26 and GrabCar Premium about RM47, with marked pickup points at the airport.
quote: Grab Car Economy costs RM26, while Grab Car Premium costs RM47 for a one-way ride to Georgetown Hotel in the city centre.

claim: PEN to George Town is about 18–20 km and 25–40 minutes by car; metered taxis use a voucher counter with a 50% midnight–6am surcharge, while public buses 102/401/401E take 45–70 minutes.
quote: The airport is approximately 18-20 km from George Town, with travel times typically ranging from 25-40 minutes by car or taxi... +50% surcharge midnight-6am... Routes: Bus 102, 401, or 401E available.

claim: The free Rapid Penang CAT shuttle loops 19 stops between the Jetty and KOMTAR every 10–15 minutes from 06:00 to 23:45 daily; a full loop takes about 40 minutes.
quote: Service runs from 6:00am to 11:45pm daily... Every 10 minutes during peak hours... Every 15 minutes at all other times... an entire loop of the Free CAT bus should take around 40 minutes.

claim: The iconic old Penang ferries were retired and replaced; new pedestrian/motorcycle-only ferries run every 20–30 minutes 06:30–23:30 across the 3 km strait for RM2 adult, RM1 child, with cashless-only ticketing.
quote: The first ferry departs Butterworth at 6:30am and the last service leaves George Town at 11:30pm. They run every 30 minutes, or every 20 minutes during weekday rush hour... Adult: RM2... the ticket office doesn't take cash.

claim: Five retired iconic Penang ferries are being repurposed — including the Pulau Pinang as a ferry museum and others as floating restaurants and art spaces — after the 2020s switch to water-bus style vessels.
quote: five of the iconic Penang ferries would be transformed into floating attractions—the Pulau Pinang into a ferry museum, the Pulau Kapas and Pulau Payar into floating restaurants.

claim: George Town in June averages highs of 31.6°C and lows of 25.5°C with rain on roughly 21.7 days; it falls in the Southwest Monsoon shoulder with afternoon showers rather than peak rainy season.
quote: the average high-temperature and low-temperature in June are 31.6°C (88.9°F) and 25.5°C (77.9°F) respectively. In George Town, during June, the rain falls for 21.7 days.

claim: The best time to visit Penang is the December–March dry season; June is off-peak with lower hotel rates and lighter crowds at heritage spots.
quote: the best time to visit Penang is during the dry season, from December to March... popular spots like George Town feel less crowded during June. Accommodation costs are lower.

claim: Gurney Drive is the modern seafront strip with luxury malls and the new 131-acre Gurney Bay park — a flashier alternative to the heritage core for nightlife and shopping.
quote: Once a quiet colonial beachfront, Gurney Drive has evolved into a 'Millionaire's Row' defined by glittering condominiums, massive luxury malls, and a newly developed 131-acre waterfront park called Gurney Bay.

claim: The UNESCO core zone packs four main heritage streets — including Lebuh Chulia, Lebuh Armenian and Lebuh Acheh — and over 1,700 historic buildings into an easily walkable grid with arcaded five-foot-ways shading pedestrians.
quote: The Core Zone contains more than 1,700 historic buildings aligned on four main streets and several perpendicular streets including Lebuh Chulia, Lebuh Armenian and Lebuh Acheh.

claim: Backdoor Bodega at 37 Jalan Gurdwara is an award-winning speakeasy ranked #52 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2024, hidden behind a clothing store with ever-changing menus.
quote: Backdoor Bodega - Address: 37 Jalan Gurdwara, George Town, 10300 Penang. Notable: Award-winning speakeasy ranked #52 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2024; hidden behind a clothing store with ever-changing menus.

claim: Good Friends Club at 39 Jalan Gurdwara sits behind teal doors with a 'Good Friends Never Bojio' shophouse sign, serving kopitiam-inspired cocktails like Laksa Negroni and Penang White Curry.
quote: Good Friends Club - Address: 39, Jalan Gurdwara, 10300 George Town, Penang - Specialty: Nostalgic cocktails inspired by kopitiam culture, including Laksa Negroni and Penang White Curry

claim: Magazine 63 at 63 Jalan Magazine is one of Penang's earliest speakeasies, hidden behind a row of nondescript shophouses next to a Da Ma Cai lottery shop, open 7pm-midnight Tue-Sun.
quote: Magazine 63 is located at 63, Jalan Magazine, 10300 George Town... was one of the very first speakeasies in Penang and sparked the hidden bar trend in the city. The bar is open from 7pm to 12am from Tuesdays to Sundays.

claim: Out of Nowhere is a speakeasy entered through a large orange fridge behind the counter of Hold Up Cafe, working from 8 signature cocktails using local fruits and ingredients like pandan, nutmeg and bunga kantan.
quote: Out of Nowhere moonlights as a minimalist coffee shop by day, and a vibrant speakeasy by night. The speakeasy is accessed through a hidden entrance—a large orange fridge located behind the counter of Hold Up Cafe.

claim: Good Friends Club is open 8pm-1am, Magazine 63 opens 8pm-3am closed Mondays, and signature drinks include laksa negroni (RM45) and milo peng (RM30).
quote: Good Friends Club features an auto garage-door entrance... Signature drinks include laksa negroni (RM45) and milo peng (RM30). Opens 8PM–1AM. Magazine 63, Penang's first speakeasy... Opens 8PM–3AM (closed Mondays).

claim: Three Sixty atop the Bayview Hotel at 25-A Lebuh Farquhar combines a revolving restaurant with a spacious outdoor sky bar offering 360-degree views over UNESCO George Town and the port.
quote: Three Sixty, found on top of the Bayview Hotel in George Town, offers a fantastic and dual rooftop setting, including both a revolving restaurant and a stylish rooftop bar. It is surrounded with breathtaking 360° views over the UNESCO World Heritage George Town

claim: The Rainbow Skywalk at The Top Komtar sits 249m up on the 68th floor, open daily 10am-10pm, with Coco Cabana bar and bistro providing refreshments on the deck.
quote: Suspended at an awe-inspiring height of 249 meters on the 68th floor of Komtar Tower... open daily from 10:00am to 10:00pm. The Coco Cabana bar and bistro provides refreshments coupled with a spectacular backdrop.

claim: Soundmaker Studio at 1st Floor No 18 Lebuh Bishop is northern Malaysia's most prominent alternative music club, hosting punk, metal and experimental gigs that typically run weekends from afternoon through before midnight.
quote: Soundmaker is a haven for alternative, punk, metal, and experimental music lovers—it's raw, loud, and unforgettable. Shows are often on weekends and start in the afternoon to end before midnight

claim: China House on Beach Street is a compound of three heritage buildings linked by an open-air courtyard with 14 spaces; The Canteen at the rear offers live jazz, indie and soul music every night of the week.
quote: China House is a traditional compound of 3 heritage buildings, linked by an open air courtyard and converted into 14 spaces... The Canteen... offers a mix of jazz, indie and soul music... live music every single night of the week.

claim: China House serves around 50 different cakes and desserts daily prepared by ten bakers, with Sun-Thu hours 9am-midnight and Fri-Sat 9am-1am, making it a viable late-evening dessert stop.
quote: Between them, you can expect 50 different cakes and desserts every day, prepared by ten bakers eager to showcase new recipes.

claim: Mugshot Cafe at 302 Lebuh Chulia stays open until midnight on Saturday and Sunday (8am-10pm weekdays), known for fresh-baked bagels and a mugshot-themed photo wall.
quote: 8am – 10pm (Mon – Fri), 8am – 12am (Sat – Sun)

claim: Chulia Street Night Hawkers operates Saturdays roughly 6pm to midnight and is reportedly lively and safe even at 11pm, making it a convenient post-dinner snack walk.
quote: Chulia Street Night Hawkers operates on Saturdays from 6:00 pm to 12:00 am... The street is lively even at 23:00 and safe, according to visitor reports.

claim: George Town's historic centre is one of Malaysia's safer travel zones but quieter side lanes feel less comfortable after bars close, and Grab is the easiest late-night option costing roughly S$2 for a short ride.
quote: George Town is one of the safest places for travelers... quieter side streets lose that comfortable feel late at night... Grab is widely used and is usually the easiest option for visitors... costing around S$2 for a short 10-minute ride

claim: Mish Mash on Muntri Street has anchored George Town's drinking scene since 2014 with craft cocktails, craft beers and an extensive single-malt whisky list.
quote: Mish Mash has been at the forefront of George Town's drinking scene since 2014, offering mean cocktails, craft beers, and an impressive selection of international single malt whiskeys.
